Responses were allowable from business owners, decision makers, and employees of the following contractor groups: HVAC/R mechanics, installers, or technicians; electricians; insulation workers (floor, ceiling, and walls); plumbers; building performance specialists; weatherization technicians; general contractors; remodeling contractors; solar installers; and energy auditors, HERS raters, and energy consultants. The survey was promoted through professional contacts, industry organizations’ blogs and newsletters, and national conferences as an effort to amass broad geographic representation of respondents. Detailed descriptors of survey respondents are included in the results section of this report. Contractors were recruited through targeted online outreach, including trade-related newsletters, trade-specific articles, and affiliated events. To gain a broader geographic region, Midwest Energy Efficiency Alliance was hired to conduct survey outreach through their newsletters and network with the Southeast Energy Efficiency Alliance, South-central Partnership for Energy Efficiency as a Resource, and Northeast Energy Efficiency Partnerships. 3.2 Materials and Procedure The final survey was designed to be completed online within 10–15 minutes and consisted of 40 questions, including one attention check embedded to ensure quality and remove bots. Response formats included Likert scales, multiple choice, ranking, and open text as applicable to each question. Survey questions focused on understanding how employers engage with the labor and training market, employers’ priorities in a new hire, and factors that influence hiring and training decisions. Some firmographic and demographic information was also collected, including the size of the firm, sector of energy efficiency, types of buildings serviced, age, race, gender, and geographic location. 6 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Hosted and administered on the Alchemer platform, the survey was available in English and designed to be accessible from both desktop and mobile devices. Important information was presented to participants on the survey landing page, including the purpose of the research, the predicted risks and benefits of participating, how the collected information would be used, and contact information for researchers and the institutional review board for questions and concerns. The participants were then asked to consent to the survey before proceeding. For those who did not consent, the survey ended immediately. Open responses were analyzed for themes using a thematic analysis and open coding. For questions about whether to train or hire, responses were bifurcated into hiring or training categories. When responses were too vague about whether they were responding to hiring or training, they were omitted. The codebooks for each question’s analysis are found in Appendix A. A complete list of survey questions is available in Appendix C. 7 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4 Survey Findings 4.1 Respondent Demographics Survey respondents reflect a relatively diverse cross section of the building trades workforce. Most respondents identified as male, with about one-third identifying as female. Respondents consisted of predominantly white and Black/African American respondents, with a smaller representation from Asian, Native Hawaiian, Hispanic, and other racial and ethnic groups.
